answer: Epoch-Linked Behavioural Prism Rule. Each identity's action history is hashed per epoch into a prism signature; admission to epoch N requires that signature to remain a bounded transformation of its prior-epoch signature, permitting slow drift but rejecting sharp discontinuities. Any new identity must build a ripple of consistent signatures across several epochs before it gains weight, so a fresh sybil pays the cost of sustained coherence rather than a one-time fee. Fabricated histories are checked against a fable of cross-epoch continuity, and inconsistent accounts are zeroed.
